title: Strict transforms under a composition of blow-ups
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, and put $b_0:S_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(S)\to S$ [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Let $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_{S_1}$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, and put $b_1:S_2=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(S_1)\to S_1$. Let $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal equipped with an isomorphism $S_2\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(S)$ over $S$ identifying $b_0b_1$ with the blow-up map. Assume the equality of subsets $V(\mathcal K)=V(\mathcal I)\cup b_0(V(\mathcal J))$. For every scheme morphism $X\to S$, let $X_1$ be its strict transform along $b_0$, and let $X_2$ be the strict transform of $X_1\to S_1$ along $b_1$ [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Under the specified isomorphism and the associative identification of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], $X_2$ is canonically isomorphic to the strict transform of $X\to S$ along $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(S)\to S$, compatibly with the closed inclusions into $X\times_S S_2$ and the projections to $X$ and $S_2$.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, clause (2) (scheme strict transforms). The support equality of the three centers is part of its hypotheses.

proof.text: Put $A=X\times_SS_1$, $B=X\times_SS_2=A\times_{S_1}S_2$, and let $M,N$ be the successive module transforms of $\mathcal O_X$ [def-trf-module-strict-transform]. By [lem-trf-iterated-transform-quotient-support], they are quasi-coherent and the canonical quotient $\alpha:\mathcal O_B\twoheadrightarrow N$ has kernel $H$ supported on $T_I\cup T_J$, with the notation of that node. Let $G$ be the module transform for the specified composite centre; its canonical quotient is $\beta:\mathcal O_B\twoheadrightarrow G$.

The support assumption gives $T=(b_0b_1f_2)^{-1}V(\mathcal K)=T_I\cup T_J$. For $s\in S_2$ with $b_0b_1(s)\notin V(\mathcal I)$, the complement isomorphism [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] gives a unique lift to $S_1$, so $b_0b_1(s)\in b_0(V(\mathcal J))$ iff $b_1(s)\in V(\mathcal J)$. Over $V(\mathcal I)$ both unions contain $s$. Pull the equality back along $f_2:B\to S_2$.

source.place: Tag 080I, displayed equality of support unions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-iterated-transform-exceptional-support] with $b=b_0$, $c=b_1$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$. Its exceptional subset $f_2^{-1}b_1^{-1}(V(\mathcal J)\cup b_0^{-1}V(\mathcal I))$ is $T_J\cup T_I=T$. Thus $N$ has no nonzero local sections vanishing off $T$.

source.place: Tag 080I, last three sentences of proof; Tag 080H comparison.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel], $\ker\beta$ consists of all local sections of $\mathcal O_B$ vanishing off $T$, so $H\subseteq\ker\beta$. The quotient property gives $\gamma:N\to G$ with $\beta=\gamma\alpha$. It is surjective on stalks since $\beta$ is. Off $T$, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are isomorphisms, so every local section of $\ker\gamma$ vanishes there. Step 3 makes it zero; thus $\gamma$ is injective and $H=\ker\beta$. These are ideals since multiplication preserves vanishing off $T$.

By [lem-trf-iterated-transform-structure-algebra], $N=k_{2,*}\mathcal O_{X_2}$ as a quotient algebra of $\mathcal O_B$, and $H$ is its defining ideal. The scheme clause of [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] identifies $G$ with the structure-algebra quotient for the composite scheme transform. Step 4 gives equal defining ideals. On $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset B$, both closed subschemes are therefore $\operatorname{Spec}(C/H)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; local identity maps agree on overlaps and glue. The resulting isomorphism commutes with inclusion into $B$, hence with both projections [def-pc-fibre-product], under the specified blow-up isomorphism.
